rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: San Francisco landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue for damages, an injunction and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month of use per affected unit may be a separate violation
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in San Francisco. The ban applies to anyone selling or using qualifying algorithmic devices, and no building-type limits are stated.
rules.penalty: Civil action by a tenant or the City Attorney for damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Each month of use for each affected unit may count as a separate violation (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C(b), (d)).
rules.conflict_note: A news article (X-santa-monica) says San Francisco banned the software in July 2023. Official sources say the Board of Supervisors approved the legislation in July 2024 and that it took effect 2024-10-14. The official dates are used here.
rules.reason: All five candidates describe the same San Francisco ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting devices (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C), so they were merged, citing the official D081 text.
